source.title: DWMGrad: an innovative neural network optimization approach using dynamic window data for adaptive updating of momentum and learning rate
source.authors: Zhi-Feng Wang; Longlong Li; Chun-Yan Zeng

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper. Some figure text is garbled, but the relevant optimizer comparison tables and descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers using held-out task performance, a different experimental setup from the claim versions. Its comparisons do not test the versions’ specific conditions and baselines.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out performance for several optimizers, but the image and language tables compare adaptive optimizers with one another, not with SGD. Its only SGD comparison is on audio tasks, outside V4’s stated image and language setting. It does not test the other versions’ interventions or measurements.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks a proposed optimizer but does not test any listed version. Image and language experiments lack an SGD baseline; the only adaptive-versus-SGD comparison concerns audio classification, outside V4's stated setting. Comparisons between Adam and AdamW alone do not establish recovery of an SGD performance advantage. No experiments test V1–V3 or V5–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors claim superior or competitive DWMGrad performance across tasks and acknowledge that their convex convergence analysis may not apply directly to non-convex deep learning. Their stronger language about consistent superiority exceeds the tables: DWMGrad loses several GLUE comparisons and does not lead every audio or graph metric.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes DWMGrad and compares it with several optimizers on image, language, graph, and audio tasks; it does not use the claim versions’ stated methods or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differing optimizer performance across datasets and architectures, including a faster Cora GAT runtime and no runtime advantage on other listed task-architecture combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 3–8 compare adaptive optimizers on image, language, and graph tasks. DWMGrad often performs best but has exceptions; these comparisons lack SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers varies across tasks and architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 9 reports UrbanSound8K accuracy: SGD versus Adam is 95.08% versus 90.45% on CAM++, 86.32% versus 92.12% on TDNN, and 73.57% versus 90.19% on Res2net. The tuning protocol is insufficiently described to establish limited tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On audio classification, adaptive optimizers can outperform or underperform SGD depending on the architecture.

record.problems: The paper reports task accuracy and related metrics rather than train-test gaps. The image and language optimizer tables do not include SGD; the audio comparison is outside V4’s stated task scope. The supplied text does not describe hyperparameter tuning sufficiently to establish a limited-tuning comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted because the reported optimizer comparisons do not test a claim version under its stated conditions and comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance using the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance on image or language benchmarks under limited tuning; effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching to SGD on that comparison.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification and V4 tested_not_extracted status should be corrected. Empty rows and labels are appropriate for these versions. Train-test gaps are not required to test V4; the decisive issues are the missing image/language SGD comparison and the audio comparison's different task scope.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization on the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The image and language comparisons do not include SGD; limited tuning and training performance comparisons are not reported. The SGD comparison is on audio tasks, outside the version’s stated image and language setting.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
